newsitem.title: GERMANY: Juncker says France wants cooperation not spending.
newsitem.headline: Juncker says France wants cooperation not spending.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker told German radio on Monday he thought France did not want expensive new European spending programmes, rather more co-ordination of economic policies.

"I have not heard that France wants expensive financial measures to be funded out of the European budget. That is not the case, particularly because the German Finance Minister (Theo Waigel) has made it clear that is out of the question," Juncker told Berlin's InfoRadio.

"We are discussing how the economic policies of the various member states of the European Union can be co-ordinated more strongly," Juncker said, as EU leaders gathered in Amsterdam for a two-day summit.
The summit has been overshadowed by a Franco-German rift over the new French government's insistence on putting more emphasis on jobs in the drive towards economic and monetary union (EMU).
Juncker said leaders were studying ways of boosting industry research and high technology development, but said there could be no new spending programmes to create jobs.
